atAGlance: Bánh mì heo quay is roast-pork bánh mì, bringing crackling pork into Vietnam’s French-influenced street sandwich with pickles, cucumber, cilantro, and chili.
whatItIs: Bánh mì heo quay makes roast pork with crisp skin the star. The best bite has crackling, rich pork, sharp pickles, cucumber, cilantro, and a little chili if you want heat.
howToEnjoy: Eat it soon so the crackling stays crisp against the bread. Ask for no chili before the vendor adds chili or spicy seasoning.
howLocalsOrder: Order bánh mì heo quay when you want crunch from roast pork skin. Ask for extra pickles or no chili early, because bánh mì stalls move quickly and the sandwich is assembled in seconds.
worthKnowing: Heo quay means roast pork; inside bánh mì, it shows Vietnam’s habit of adapting the loaf to local appetites. Crackling, herbs, and đồ chua make it feel more Vietnamese than a simple roast-pork sandwich.
